questions.question: What is the correct order of the five steps in the writing process?
questions.explanation: The writing process starts with prewriting (planning), then drafting, revising (improving content), editing (fixing language) and finally publishing.

questions.question: What is the main focus of the revising step?
questions.explanation: Revising is about improving content and structure, while editing comes later and focuses on grammar, spelling and punctuation.

questions.question: Which of these is a prewriting technique?
questions.explanation: Brainstorming, mind mapping, freewriting and outlining are all prewriting techniques used to gather and organise ideas before writing.

questions.question: Which question belongs on an editing checklist?
options: Is the subject in agreement with the verb (he goes, not he go)?
Do I have enough ideas for my topic?
Should I add another main character?
questions.explanation: Editing deals with language details such as capital letters, spelling, verb tenses and subject-verb agreement.

questions.question: What often happens when students skip planning and revising?
options: The text lacks clear structure and contains many language errors
The text automatically becomes shorter and better
The text gets a better structure
questions.explanation: Skipping steps in the writing process often leads to texts without clear structure, few details, repetition and many language errors.
